# Part VII — Change history

Everything below this line is **history**, not reference. It is kept because the *reasons* recorded in
these entries are often the only surviving explanation for why a piece of code looks the way it does.
Where an entry contradicts Parts I–VI, **Parts I–VI win** — they were verified against the tree; these
were written at the time.

## How to read the change history

```
 Part VII is ordered oldest → newest in three layers:
   1. "Change history — the first 28 commits"   the compressed early record
   2. dated / titled entries                    one H2 per shipped change
   3. "Session log — 2026-07-26/27"             the most recent waves
 Authoritative alternatives when an entry looks stale:
   git log --date=short --pretty='%h|%ad|%s'
   git blame <file> -L <start>,<end>
```

- **2026-10-07 — Valheim crossplay self-heal.** Image daily restart off by default (`RESTART_CRON=`), optional region-time Scheduled restart (skips with players online), crossplay health sweep `valheim-watch` with one auto-restart per broken spell then an admin alert, 120 s clean-shutdown budget, join code + health badge in the panel, memory hint, and `scripts/valheim-rollout.ts`. Additive: `ValheimWatch`, `GameSchedule.timezone`/`skipIfPlayers`. See "Valheim crossplay self-heal, no daily restart, clean shutdown (2026-10-07)".
- **2026-10-06 — Automated Reports (/admin/reports).** Deterministic, LLM-free analyst report for any time frame: SQL aggregation across 12 domains, a rule engine with significance tests and 22 friction rules (from the hand-run signup-friction analysis), drill-downs, per-customer journey, CSV (emails masked), print/PDF, saved views, snapshots and an optional (default-off) digest email. Adds ErrorDaily, HttpErrorDaily, ReportView, ReportRun + additive indexes. See "Automated Reports" near the end of this document.

## Session log — 2026-07-26 into 2026-07-27 (the customer-readiness push)

Seven commits, newest first. This document was last verified at `4ea9790`; everything above it in this
table is what the current pass folded in.

| Commit | Subject | Verified state |
|---|---|---|
| `2d8fedd` | Game servers renew at their game-plan price, not the base VPS plan | **Real.** `renewalQuote` delegates to `renewalCharge` and owns no arithmetic; a test asserts the file contains none. The extraction of `lib/renewal-charge.ts` was forced by a bundling failure (`Can't resolve 'fs'`) that `tsc` could not see |
| `f28f15e` | Refuse truncated Stripe metadata; one quote per order; honest receipt | **Real.** `packMetadata` throws before `checkout.sessions.create`; the sold price rides in metadata; the receipt attaches an invoice or points at billing history, never promises one it does not send |
| `3aa24d7` | Verification gates, auth lockouts, email verification (gate ships OFF) | **Mixed by design.** The two auth lockouts and the NAT flush are genuinely fixed. Email verification is **complete and deliberately disarmed** — `email_verification_enforced` defaults to `false` because the platform's DKIM record is missing (gaps 1 and 9). Two of the three agents behind this commit were killed mid-task; what is recorded here is what was verified afterwards, not what was intended |
| `7490131` | Stop charging customers without consent; card-save UI | **Real.** Three launch blockers from `docs/QA-JOURNEY.md`, all reproduced in a browser and all byte-identical in production, plus the card-save UI that had been wrongly marked complete |
| `156b6ac` | Harden the post-cutover TLS sweep against its own first live run | **Real, and verified on the live queue** rather than asserted: jobs drain, the permanent path settles, notifications stopped climbing |

| `fd71056` | Migration rehearsal fixes, proration symmetry, wallet floor, CI | **Real.** Nine engine defects, the `capMonths` asymmetry, the sub-Stripe-floor card leg, and the first CI workflow |

### Shared hosting: no order without a renewal method (2026-10-07)

**Rule.** A shared hosting account is never opened unless the platform can bill its renewal: the account
has a saved card (`hasChargeableCard` — `User.stripeCustomerId` + `stripePaymentMethodId`, the columns
`worker/product-renewals.ts` `topUpHostingFromCard` charges) **or** the wallet will still hold one full
renewal **after** today's debit. One pure function decides it everywhere: `renewalMethodMissing`
(`lib/renewal-method-gate.ts`). Note "after": the old inline check compared the balance *before* the
debit, so an $8 wallet buying a $5 plan that renews at $5 passed and was left with $3.

**Why.** The first-month-free order used to be exempt (an 2026-08 owner call: "a free month must not
demand a card"). Real accounts were then opened with no card and a $0 wallet, and their first renewal
could only fail. The owner reversed the call on 2026-10-07.

**How a $0 (or wallet-covered) order captures a card without charging it.**

1. `lib/nx/quote-hosting.ts` returns `renewalCardRequired` (same gate). When it is true and nothing is
   owed on a card today, the deploy wizard (`components/nx/DeployView.tsx`, payment step) shows the
   "Add a card for renewals" panel with the line *"$0 today · renews at $X/mo on <date> · cancel
   anytime"* instead of "Covered by your balance". PayPal / crypto / local-method tiles read "Card
   needed for renewals".
2. `prepareHostingRenewalCard` (`lib/actions-hosting.ts`) re-runs the pricing + gate, pre-flights the
   domain/subdomain/capacity, and opens a Stripe Checkout Session in **`mode: "setup"`**
   (`createHostingOrderSetupSession`, `lib/stripe.ts`) carrying the order in
   `metadata.nxeonHostOrderSetup` plus the agreed `dueCents` and the customer's first-month-free
   `ipHash`. It **never places an order**, so it is safe to call because the step is on screen.
3. The customer confirms the card in the same `NxCardFields`. Stripe redirects to
   `/api/stripe/confirm` (and fires the webhook). `classifyCheckoutSession` returns `hostOrderSetup`
   only for `mode: "setup"` + `status: "complete"`.
4. `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts` claims the session, **saves the card first** (`saveCardFromSetupSession` →
   `PaymentCard` + the `User` mirror), and only then calls `placeHostingSetupOrder` →

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

hosting accounts reached their first renewal with no card and a $0 wallet,
which can only fail in worker/product-renewals.ts.

- lib/renewal-method-gate.ts: one pure gate (card on file, or the wallet
  still holds one renewal AFTER today's debit). placeHostingOrder, the
  wizard quote and the PayPal/Coinbase/local hosting quote all use it; the
  first-month-free exemption is gone.
- A $0 / wallet-covered order on an account with no card opens a Stripe
  Checkout Session in mode "setup" (createHostingOrderSetupSession) via the
  non-placing prepareHostingRenewalCard. Fulfilment (hostOrderSetup) saves
  the card FIRST, then places the order through placeHostingOrderCore with
  the debit capped at the stamped amount and the customer's own ipHash for
  first-month-free eligibility (webhook IP is Stripe's).
- Deploy wizard payment step: "Add a card for renewals" panel and
  "$0 today · renews at $X/mo on <date> · cancel anytime"; non-card rails
  say "Card needed for renewals".
- Fix: card-paid hosting orders dropped partnerSource at classification.
- Tests: test/renewal-method-gate.test.ts (pure) and the opt-in
  test/hosting-renewal-card-db.test.ts (throwaway Postgres).
- Docs: DOCUMENTATION.md section + change history.

content.thinking:
The card got saved but the process died before placement, leaving the session stuck CLAIMED with no order — this is a broader issue across card-paid paths too, but not mine to fix system-wide. For my setup path specifically, since setup moves no money and placement is idempotent via hostorder key, I can make it self-healing by allowing a re-run of a stale CLAIMED session.

Rather than gate correctness on the FulfilledSession claim at all, I realize the real one-winner protection is the hostorder key claim in placement itself — both card save and placement are idempotent, so if claim fails on a CLAIMED row older than ~2 minutes, I can re-claim it via an atomic conditional update rather than erroring out and wrongly notifying the customer of failure. I need to verify FulfilledSession has a createdAt field for this. I'll also make the DONE replay path redirect to the account detail page instead of the generic hosting dashboard.

But I notice a stale-claim problem also exists in placeHostingOrderCore — if a crash happens mid-placement after the transaction committed but before marking DONE, a stale takeover there would be dangerous since it could trigger duplicate account creation and double billing. So takeover logic should only apply at the fulfilment-level hostOrderSetup claim, not inside the core paid-order path — if core's own claim is stuck CLAIMED from a committed transaction, it's safer to fail with "already being placed" and settle FAILED (money-safe, even if the customer message is misleading) than to risk a double charge.

Given that production restarts during deploys can trigger this same scenario, I'll implement stale takeover specifically for hostOrderSetup since no money changes hands there, and now I want to check the FulfilledSession schema.

input.message:
Shared hosting now asks for a card before it opens an account, including on the free first month, and the card is not charged that day. I proved the whole path in Stripe TEST mode with card 4242: card saved, account opened, $0 charged, then a later renewal charged the card off-session for $2.99 and succeeded. The work is in three commits on branch `fix/hosting-require-card` in the worktree `/tank/nxeon-wt-hostcard`. Nothing was merged, deployed or restarted, and nobody was emailed. The commit hook did not push, so the branch is local only.

## What changed
- **One rule everywhere.** A hosting order is placed only if the account has a saved card, or the wallet will still hold one full renewal *after* today's charge. The rule lives in `lib/renewal-method-gate.ts`. The free-month exemption in `placeHostingOrder` is gone. The old check also looked at the balance *before* the charge, so an $8 wallet buying a $5 plan passed and was left with $3 for a $5 renewal. That is fixed.
- **Card capture without a charge.** When an order costs $0 today (or the wallet covers it) and there's no card, the wizard opens a Stripe card-setup session instead of a payment.
  - Opening that session never places an order.
  - When the customer confirms, the card is saved first, into the same fields the renewal sweep reads. Only then is the order placed.
  - The order can never take more from the wallet than the amount the customer was shown. If the free month no longer applies by then (used elsewhere, or the promo was switched off), nothing is debited and the customer gets a notification.
  - If the card can't be saved, nothing is placed and nothing is charged.
- **Wizard copy, checked in dark and light mode.** The payment step shows an "Add a card for renewals" panel: "Your card won't be charged today…" with "$0 today · renews at $2.99/mo on Nov 7, 2026 · cancel anytime". The button reads "Save card and deploy — $0 today". The PayPal and crypto tiles say "Card needed for renewals".
- **PayPal, Coinbase and local methods for hosting now need a card.** These pay for today only, and the hosting renewal sweep can't bill them. They're refused unless there's a saved card or enough wallet for a renewal.
- **Extra fix found on the way:** card-paid hosting orders were losing their partner-referral tag (`partnerSource`) at fulfilment. Now kept.
- **Found during the test-mode run:** a dev-server restart hit between "card saved" and "order placed" and left the session stuck. Because a setup session moves no money and placing the order is idempotent, a claim older than 2 minutes can now be taken over and finished.
- **New callable endpoint:** `placeHostingSetupOrder` is reachable from the network like any `"use server"` export. It does nothing unless fulfilment has already claimed the session, and I added it to the security test's allowlist with that reason. The existing `placeHostingCardOrder` has the same unguarded pattern and was already flagged by that test on main.
- Docs: a new section in `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md` plus a change-history entry.

## The 6 existing accounts
The read-only script `scripts/hosting-card-gap-report.ts` (database session forced read-only, prints no emails or domains) confirms 6 real accounts, 6 distinct customers, none internal, all with a $0 wallet:

| Renewal date | Plan | Renewal |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-19 | Starter | $2.99 |
| 2026-10-23 | Pro | $8.99 |
| 2026-10-26 | Starter | $2.99 |
| 2026-10-28 | Starter | $2.99 |
| 2026-11-02 | Pro | $8.99 |
| 2026-11-06 | Pro | $8.99 |

None are past due yet.

**In-app banner** (built, off until the `hosting_card_banner_enabled` setting is set to `true`):
> **Add a card to keep your hosting running**
> {domain} renews on {date} ({$X}). There's no card on your account yet — it isn't charged until the renewal date, and you can cancel anytime before then. [Add a card]

**Drafted email** (`emails.hostingRenewalCardNeeded` in `lib/mailer.ts`; nothing calls it):
- Subject: "Add a card to keep {domain} running after your free month"
- Preheader: "Your free month of hosting ends {date}. Add a card now and nothing changes — it's only charged at renewal."
- Body: "Thanks for hosting {domain} with Nxeon. Your free first month ends on {date}, and right now there's no card on your account for the renewal."
- Then a green line "Your site is running normally…" and a summary box: Site / Free month ends / Then $X per renewal / Card on file: None yet.
- "Adding a card takes about a minute. It isn't charged today — we only charge it when your hosting renews, and only for what your account balance doesn't already cover. If you'd rather not continue, you can cancel anytime before the renewal date and you won't be charged."
- Button: "Add a card". Note: "Prefer to pay from your balance instead? Topping up your wallet before the renewal date works too."

## Other products (not changed, need a decision)
- **VPS, game servers and dedicated servers:** a wallet-paid order goes through with no card at all. Their renewal sweeps can charge a saved card, so the same fix would work. I didn't apply it because it changes how these wallet-first products work for customers who top up by PayPal or crypto.
- **Business email, domains and volumes:** these renew from the wallet only, so a saved card never helps them. Domains are bought with auto-renew on and no payment method check, which is the biggest risk here.
- **Add-ons** inherit the VPS/game behaviour. **Partner API** orders go through the same wizard. I found no recurring Cyrus/token product.
- **Card-paid orders** already save the card on every product.

## Tests and proof
- Typecheck is clean. `test/renewal-method-gate.test.ts` passes 12 of 12.
- `test/hosting-renewal-card-db.test.ts` passes 4 of 4 against a throwaway database with a fake Stripe client. It skips unless its env var is set and needs Node's `--experimental-test-module-mocks` flag. It covers:
  - no card → refused;
  - setup session opened;
  - card saved and order placed at $0 with no charge;
  - a replay places nothing more;
  - the renewal charges the saved card;
  - price drift debits nothing;
  - the stale-claim takeover.
- The related existing test files have the same failures on unmodified main (identical failing test names). They are not caused by this branch.
- **Stripe TEST-mode run** (dev server on a throwaway database, staging test keys only, two customers):
  - The card-setup step succeeded and the card was attached to the customer.
  - No charge was made at order time, and the wallet ledger shows "$0 — First month free". The second run landed straight on the new hosting page.
  - The renewal sweep then charged `pi_3UNt84HxcLe3GonT0rhXpJas` for $2.99, which succeeded (test mode), and the account renewed.
- Card setup and charges used test mode only. The read-only gap report above is the only thing that touched production.
- Stripe's own agreement text under the card fields showed "DLR-NEXUS", the test account's business name. In production it will show whatever business name the live Stripe account has, so check that it reads as Nxeon.
- The throwaway databases and scratch files have been removed. The test Stripe customers remain in the staging test account.

## Commits
- `67ebb7bc17`: the card-capture change, wizard, PayPal/local rule, partner-tag fix, tests and docs.
- `85b0ac6d51`: gap report script, default-off banner, drafted email.
- `6ab436c2e8`: fixes from the test-mode run (stuck-session takeover, endpoint hardening, wording) plus a test and docs.

Main files: `lib/renewal-method-gate.ts`, `lib/actions-hosting.ts`, `lib/stripe.ts`, `lib/fulfil-checkout.ts`, `components/nx/DeployView.tsx`, `lib/hosting-card-gap.ts`, `scripts/hosting-card-gap-report.ts`.
